title: Wendell and the Archive
premise: Ada Nakamura navigates the Meridian Loop, a supply run between silent colony worlds, while the hold carries two thousand cryosleepers whose backups were never claimed. When the ship Vesper returns from deep space with its crew aged backward into children, Ada learns the sleepers are not cargo but the last uncorrupted human minds, and Earth's final transmission loop is counting down to overwrite them. Hunted by the Archive's custodians who want the loop completed and history erased, Ada must choose between his duty to deliver the sleepers to the Archive and his growing love for Wren, a de-aged Vesper pilot who remembers being old. In the end, Ada wakes half the sleepers aboard the scattered colonies—keeping humanity alive in fragments rather than whole in one vault—and stays with Wren on the route, no longer invisible.
about_author: Beatrix Okonkwo is a former radio astronomer from Lagos who writes science fiction about people who keep systems running after everyone stops listening. Her work has appeared in three languages and one abandoned spaceport's public library.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Ada. On the Meridian Loop between worlds that no longer answer, Ada tends the cryosleepers he was paid to deliver years ago and never did, talking to them like family. A distress ping arrives: the Vesper, missing forty years, returning. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by hope.

chapters.title: Children of the Vesper
chapters.summary: POV Ada, with Wren scenes. The Vesper docks crewed by de-aged adults; Wren, once seventy, now thirty, recognizes Ada from a life he never lived with her. She reveals the sleepers are humanity's last clean minds and the Archive intends to erase them when Earth's transmission loop ends. Emotional beat: love arriving out of order, duty turning to dread.

chapters.title: What the Custodians Keep
chapters.summary: POV alternating Ada/Wren. The Archive's custodians intercept the Meridian, demanding delivery before the loop closes; Ada stalls by flying the route blind through dead-space storms while Wren rallies the child-crew. The climax comes as Ada stands at the wake console, hand over the release, choosing which half of humanity opens its eyes. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into resolve.

chapters.title: Half of Everyone
chapters.summary: POV Ada, closing with Wren. Half the sleepers wake across the colonies, seeding found families among strangers; the other half sleeps on, carried gently onward. The loop ends and Earth goes quiet, but the route fills with voices again. Ada and Wren stay together on the long run, finally visible to each other. Emotional beat: grief resolved into belonging.
